quick: 30 mg PO 1-3 h before sex; may increase to 60 mg (max once/24 h)
With or without food; take with a full glass of water
Caution in moderate impairment; avoid in severe
Avoid - additive CNS depression, syncope, dizziness
summary: Dapoxetine is a short-acting SSRI developed specifically for on-demand treatment of premature ejaculation in adult men. Taken 1-3 hours before intercourse, it raises the ejaculatory threshold by potentiating serotonergic neurotransmission. Its rapid absorption and short half-life suit episodic use. Key issues are orthostatic hypotension/syncope, nausea, dizziness, and dangerous interactions with MAOIs and other serotonergic or potent CYP3A4-inhibiting drugs.
indications: On-demand treatment of premature ejaculation (PE) in adult men aged 18-64 years with an intravaginal ejaculatory latency time (IELT) of less than 2 minutes and persistent/recurrent ejaculation with minimal stimulation, before/on/shortly after penetration with distress, for >=6 months

dosage.d: 30 mg taken 1-3 hours before anticipated sexual activity
dosage.n: Not more than once every 24 hours

dosage.d: Increase to 60 mg if 30 mg insufficient and tolerated
dosage.n: Max 60 mg once in any 24 hours

dosage.d: Reassess benefit/risk after the first 4 weeks (or 6 doses)

admin: Take orally 1 to 3 hours before planned sexual activity, on an as-needed basis only
Swallow with at least one full glass of water to reduce risk of syncope
Do not take more than one dose in any 24-hour period
Avoid abrupt position changes; advise the patient how to recognize prodromal symptoms of syncope
Do not combine with recreational drugs or alcohol
moa: Dapoxetine is a potent, short-acting selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor. By blocking presynaptic serotonin (5-HT) reuptake it increases serotonergic neurotransmission in the brain stem and at spinal motor neurons controlling ejaculation, raising the ejaculatory threshold and prolonging ejaculatory latency. Its rapid onset and rapid elimination make it suitable for episodic on-demand dosing rather than continuous SSRI use.

absolute: Significant pathological cardiac conditions (heart failure, conduction defects, ischemia, significant valvular disease)
History of mania/bipolar disorder or severe depression
Concurrent or recent (within 14 days) MAOIs, thioridazine, or potent CYP3A4 inhibitors
Concurrent serotonergic agents (other SSRIs/SNRIs, tricyclics, lithium, tryptophan, St John's wort, tramadol)
relative: History of syncope or orthostatic hypotension
monitor: Drugs that prolong PR/QT or affect cardiac conduction

preg: Not indicated for use in women. No relevant pregnancy use.
lact: Not indicated for use in women. No relevant lactation use.
renal: Use with caution in mild to moderate renal impairment; not recommended in severe renal impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in moderate and severe hepatic impairment due to increased exposure. Use with caution in mild impairment.

major: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors - risk of fatal serotonin syndrome; contraindicated and require 14-day washout each way
Other serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, tramadol, linezolid, lithium, St John's wort, triptans) - serotonin syndrome risk
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) - markedly increase dapoxetine levels; contraindicated
moderate: PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil) - additive orthostatic hypotension/syncope
Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (erythromycin, fluconazole, amprenavir, diltiazem) - increased exposure (limit to 30 mg)
minor: CYP2D6 inhibitors - modest increase in exposure
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; high-fat meals slightly delay absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it increases dizziness, drowsiness, syncope and neurocardiogenic effects.

serious: Mood changes / suicidal ideation (SSRI class effect)
emergency: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Orthostatic blood pressure and pulse, especially at first dose
Review concomitant serotonergic and CYP3A4-affecting medications
counsel: Take only when planning sexual activity, 1-3 hours before, no more than once a day
Take with a full glass of water and avoid alcohol
If you feel light-headed, lie down with legs raised to prevent fainting; rise slowly
Do not use with MAOIs, other antidepressants, recreational drugs, or strong antifungal/antiviral medicines
Report fainting, persistent low mood, or thoughts of self-harm
pk: Store at room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; dapoxetine is approved via EMA/national authorities in many countries (Europe, Asia) specifically for premature ejaculation - dosing and contraindications follow the SmPC
Designed as a short-acting on-demand SSRI - taken before intercourse, not as daily therapy
Contraindicated with MAOIs, other serotonergic drugs and potent CYP3A4 inhibitors; observe a 14-day washout with MAOIs
Syncope is the main safety concern - take with water, avoid alcohol, and counsel patients to lie down if light-headed
Reassess benefit-risk after the first few doses; not for men under 18 or over 64 or with significant cardiac disease
missed: Dapoxetine is taken on demand only, so there is no fixed dosing schedule and no missed dose to make up. Never take a second dose within 24 hours.
overdose: There is limited overdose experience; expect intensified adverse effects such as nausea, dizziness and syncope, and a risk of serotonin syndrome especially with other serotonergic drugs. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care, cardiac monitoring, and treat serotonin syndrome with cooling, benzodiazepines and supportive measures. Dialysis is unlikely to help (highly protein bound).
